pages.name: A square and its side
pages.text: A square of area 9 has sides of 3, because 3 × 3 = 9, so its [[square root]], `√9`, is 3. Drag the corner. At areas between 1, 4, 9, 16 and 25 the side is still a real length, written exactly as a [[surd]] such as `√7`.

pages.name: The side of 36
pages.task: A square has an area of 36. How long is its side, `√36`?
pages.why: The side times itself gives the area, and 6 × 6 = 36, so `√36 = 6`. Squaring 6 back gives 36, which checks it.

pages.name: An exact side
pages.task: A square has an area of 7 m². Which writes its side exactly?
pages.why: `√7` m times itself is exactly 7 m². 2.65 m is `√7` rounded to two places, close but not exact, since 2.65 × 2.65 = 7.0225.

pages.name: The edge of 64
pages.task: A cube has a volume of 64. How long is its edge, `∛64`?
pages.why: 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, so `∛64 = 4`. A cube root uses the edge three times, not twice.

pages.text: A square of area 48 splits into 16 small squares of area 3, 4 along each side, so its side is four `√3`s end to end: `4√3`, which means 4 × `√3`. Use the biggest square number that divides 48, trying 4, 9, 16, 25: 48 = 4 × 12 would leave a 4 inside the 12. Try 8 × 6, and the 8 squares will not make a square.

pages.text: The `√` sign is agreed to mean the positive root, the side, so `√36` is 6. But −6 × −6 is also 36, so `x² = 36` has two answers, `x = 6` or `x = −6`.

pages.task: A square plate has an area of 50 cm². What is its side, exactly?
